faq.q: Why is it hard to ask for help?
faq.a: We may worry that others will think we are silly, or that we are bothering them. Most people actually like helping, and they do not think you are silly at all.
asks: Why am I scared to ask for help?

faq.q: How do I ask for help?
faq.a: Choose someone you trust, take a breath and say, "Please can you help me? I am stuck on this part." Saying exactly what is tricky makes it easier for them to help.
asks: How do I ask my teacher for help?

faq.q: Is asking for help a sign of weakness?
faq.a: No, it is a sign of strength and good sense. Doctors, astronauts and team captains ask for help all the time. Nobody can do everything alone.
asks: Is it weak to ask for help?

faq.q: Who can I ask for help?
faq.a: A parent or carer, a teacher, a friend, an older brother or sister, or a school counsellor. For big worries, choose a grown-up you trust.
asks: Who should I go to when I need help?

faq.q: What if the person I ask is busy or says no?
faq.a: Ask again later, or ask someone else. If it is something serious, keep telling grown-ups until someone helps you.

facts: In a 2008 study, people guessed they would have to ask about twice as many strangers for help as they really needed to, because people are more helpful than we expect.
Many schools have counsellors whose job is to help children with worries and feelings.
